original_question: If P and Q are Scott sober dcpos, must their product dcpo P x Q also be Scott sober? Here Scott sober means that the Scott space of the dcpo is sober.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Question 4.6: "Let P, Q be Scott sober dcpos. Must the product P × Q be Scott sober?" This is posed immediately after Definition 4.4, which defines a dcpo P to be Scott sober iff its Scott space ΣP is sober. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
correct_elements: Your draft is already essentially the paper’s question: it asks about two Scott sober dcpos P and Q, their product P × Q, and uses the paper’s meaning of "Scott sober" as sobriety of the Scott space. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
missing_details: Make the universal quantifier explicit: for every pair of dcpos P and Q with sober Scott spaces ΣP and ΣQ, is Σ(P × Q) sober? ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

Specify that P × Q is the order-theoretic product dcpo, not the topological product of Scott spaces; this is implicit in the paper’s wording "the product P × Q" in Section 4. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

Use the paper’s notation ΣP for the Scott space if you want the question to be fully stand-alone in the paper’s language. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

Do not add extra hypotheses such as continuity, algebraicity, bounded completeness, lattice structure, or domain assumptions; Question 4.6 is stated for arbitrary Scott sober dcpos. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

The adjacent domain case is only context: the paper notes that if one factor P is a domain, then P × Q is sober for any sober dcpo Q, but that is not part of Question 4.6 itself. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
refined_question: For dcpos P and Q, suppose that their Scott spaces ΣP and ΣQ are sober. Must the order product dcpo P × Q also be Scott sober; equivalently, is the Scott space Σ(P × Q) necessarily sober? ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
equivalent_formulation: If P and Q are dcpos such that ΣP and ΣQ are sober, is Σ(P × Q) sober? This is equivalent by Definition 4.4(1). ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
justification: The exact target is Section 4, Question 4.6. The paper first introduces the terminology "Scott sober" in Definition 4.4 specifically to emphasize the Scott topology, then asks whether the product of two Scott sober dcpos is again Scott sober. I therefore kept the scope exactly at the two-factor product problem and did not broaden it to the neighboring characterization problem in Question 4.8 or the well-filtered analogue in Question 4.7. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
